name: Manchester Liberalism
summary: Manchester Liberalism, the creed of the Manchester School around Richard Cobden and John Bright, held that free trade, minimal government and low taxation would bring prosperity and, by binding nations in commerce, peace. It opposed the Corn Laws, military spending, empire and foreign intervention, and backed retrenchment, press freedom, separation of church and state and wider suffrage, while Bright rejected state regulation of factories and wages.
scope: The mid-19th-century Manchester School, the Anti-Corn Law League and its leaders Cobden and Bright, drawing on Cobden's speeches and Wikipedia and EBSCO accounts. It excludes later New Liberalism and modern neoliberalism or libertarianism that borrow the name. Cobden was somewhat more open than Bright to protective legislation for women and children.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Anachronistic; the school opposed state provision of welfare-type services as interference, though it never addressed health insurance.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Bright opposed state regulation of wages and conditions as a matter for owners and workers to settle, and Cobden held the labour market works best unfettered.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Cobden argued that prices and the labour market are set by free exchange and that interference, such as bread-tax protection, harms the public.

public-ownership.rationale: Laissez-faire economics was the school's core; state-run industry runs against its commercial and anti-state outlook (inferred, railways were then private).

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Cobden wanted lower taxes through cutting military spending rather than redistribution; he did attack landlord privilege, so only mildly negative, inferred.

unions-good.rationale: Bright opposed legislated regulation but favoured bargaining between owners and workers; the sources do not state a view on unions, and the school split on this.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property and free commerce were assumed in laissez-faire thought, though Cobden attacked landed privilege; no source states this directly.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Bright's view that government should not regulate working conditions suggests hostility to regulation of business; corporations as such were not discussed.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from laissez-faire and public thrift; the poor law is not discussed in the sources I opened, and Cobden was somewhat sympathetic to the poor.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; the school's individualist commercial liberalism implies workers' ownership is a private choice rather than a goal.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the school's liberal suspicion of state power and its hostility to the security state; terrorism-era surveillance is anachronistic.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from laissez-faire liberty and opposition to state paternalism; drug policy was not discussed.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Freedom of the press was a listed commitment, which implies opposition to legal speech restrictions; hate speech itself is anachronistic.

strong-leader.rationale: Cobden and Bright campaigned through Parliament and public agitation and attacked executive and aristocratic management of foreign policy.

state-harmful.rationale: The school favoured a minimal state but not no state; it relied on Parliament, law and retrenchment rather than abolition.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; liberal individualism and peace advocacy pull in opposite directions.

empower-police-military.rationale: Cobden called for cutting the enormous standing armaments and said England had no one to fear, so more military funding is the opposite of his programme.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from opposition to paternalist state interference; not discussed in the sources.

decide-locally.rationale: Not addressed; the school stressed Parliament and national free-trade policy but opposed central regulation of industry.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no documented position.

traditional-family.rationale: Not addressed; the school's nonconformist, middle-class liberal milieu was not a traditionalist movement.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic and undiscussed; adherents would likely tolerate it as liberty but the school took no position.

more-religion-public.rationale: The article lists separation of church and state among its commitments, and Bright favoured disestablishment.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Bright and Cobden were anti-slavery, but state programmes to correct historical injustices are anachronistic and run against laissez-faire.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cobden's cosmopolitanism and internationalism made national-culture preservation a minor concern; inferred.

gradual-change.rationale: Bright and Cobden pursued reform through Parliament and agitation, but they also demanded sweeping repeal and reform, so only mild agreement.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from free movement of goods and cosmopolitan internationalism; immigration restriction was not their issue.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Cobden favoured arbitration of disputes but wanted governments to have as little to do with each other as possible, so not stronger organisations.

free-trade.rationale: Free trade was the movement's defining cause, which Cobden and Bright pursued through the Anti-Corn Law League.

nation-first.rationale: Cobden saw free trade as uniting mankind in peace, and argued against coercion of other nations, so national interest over cooperation is rejected.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Bright and Cobden opposed military intervention abroad, as in the Crimean War, as beyond Britain's interests and capacity.

open-borders.rationale: Cobden's cosmopolitanism and free exchange suggest sympathy, but migration was not a defined plank; only trade is documented.

limit-growth.rationale: Cobden argued prosperity comes from trade and manufacturing; growth limits are anachronistic and contrary to his argument.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from laissez-faire opposition to large-scale state direction of the economy.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Industrial and commercial progress was a basis of the school's optimism, but it never made this claim directly.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis for a position.

revolution-justified.rationale: Cobden and Bright pursued reform through peaceful agitation and Parliament; Bright disliked violence, though he backed the Union in the American Civil War.

experts-over-public.rationale: The movement mobilised popular agitation and sought wider suffrage, so rule by experts contradicts its method; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Cobden argued the market is elastic if left unfettered and that free trade, not state direction, brings prosperity, so central planning is opposed.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; the school was committed to private commerce and would see public ownership as unnecessary.

land-value-tax.rationale: Cobden attacked landlords' interest in the bread tax but the sources do not show support for a land tax replacing others.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not discussed; Cobden attacked landlord privileges, but heavy taxes on inheritance run against laissez-faire; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Anachronistic; unconditional state transfers are contrary to the school's laissez-faire and retrenchment principles.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Commerce, wages and money were the basis of the school's economic order; abolition is the opposite of its laissez-faire premise.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; free-market sympathy is offset by the school's lack of monetary-theory positions.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Bright held that wages and conditions should be settled between owners and workers without state action, which excludes state-recognised bodies fixing wages and prices.

one-party-rule.rationale: The movement operated through parliamentary agitation and open campaigning, and called itself neither Whig nor Tory; single-party rule is alien to it.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Neither man campaigned against the monarchy; the movement targeted aristocratic and landed privilege, not the crown.

democracy-best.rationale: Bright campaigned for wide franchise, secret ballot and seat redistribution, but the sources do not frame democracy as best even when voters err.

direct-votes.rationale: Their reform agitation worked through Parliament and representation; referendums are not documented in the sources.

workers-councils.rationale: Council power is contrary to the school's commercial liberalism and parliamentary reformism; inferred.

right-to-secede.rationale: Bright backed the Union in the American Civil War and opposed Irish home rule as a step to independence, but Cobden had no stated position.

natural-rulers.rationale: Cobden attacked landed-aristocratic privilege and the Corn Laws that served it, rejecting the idea that a class is born to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Cobden said resisting injustice does not need arms and pointed to Quaker passive resistance; Bright was a pacifist yet supported the Union, so not absolute.

war-builds-character.rationale: Cobden denounced war and its burdens, saying no one should lend money to be applied to cutting throats.

separate-church-state.rationale: The article lists separation of church and state among the school's commitments.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Church-state separation was a commitment, so scriptural law is rejected; inferred.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Cobden wanted armaments cut sharply but still assumed government defense; private provision was not discussed.

military-superiority.rationale: Cobden proposed mutual reduction of armaments and said there is no danger of anybody coming to molest England, rejecting superiority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Cobden's cosmopolitan outlook and trade-based internationalism contradict ethnic nationhood; inferred.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Cobden framed the Corn Laws as a landlord-versus-public conflict, but the school stressed shared commercial interest rather than class struggle as the driver.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Laissez-faire liberalism seeks legal and commercial freedom, not equalised results; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Cobden opposed colonialism and the Opium War as unrighteous, but reparations were not discussed and run against retrenchment.

civilizational-union.rationale: Cobden's internationalism was based on universal trade between all nations, not on civilisational blocs; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Classical economic liberalism treated self-interest in trade as socially beneficial, but the sources do not state it as a moral claim.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The school's individualist liberalism put liberty first; inferred.

limit-population.rationale: Not discussed; the school would leave family size to individuals under laissez-faire.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Cobden held that prosperity came from trade and manufacturing and defended the industrial towns' interests.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Industrial progress underpinned the movement, but disruption of institutions as a goal is not stated; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from liberty against state interference.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from liberal suspicion of state power.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from preference for limited government and parliamentary accountability.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement attacked the landed privilege embedded in the old order, notably the Corn Laws, to achieve reform.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The movement was strongly principled, with free trade as doctrine, though it justified principle by results.

direct-action.rationale: Methods were petitioning, mass meetings and Parliament, including the Anti-Corn Law League; not insurrectionary direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Cobden's linking of peaceful means with a peaceful commercial world fits this, but he did not state it as a general principle.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Cobden championed trade and manufacturing as the source of prosperity, contrary to any return to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Division of labour was central to Smithian economics that the school turned into policy.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution by market exchange and work is the core of laissez-faire; inferred.

production-for-use.rationale: The school sought commerce driven by price and profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Classical liberal economics held profit as a legitimate return in a free market; inferred.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Class dictatorship contradicts the school's commitment to liberty and parliamentary methods.

collective-farming.rationale: Inferred from private property and commerce; Cobden addressed tenant farmers in terms of free trade.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Cobden argued the reverse, that free trade would unite mankind in the bonds of peace and unify nations.

taxation-theft.rationale: The movement wanted taxes reduced and cut through retrenchment, but accepted taxes as legitimate ("taxes they are").

harm-principle.rationale: Inferred from liberal opposition to paternalist interference; the school did not formulate the principle.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Inferred from individualist liberalism; not stated in the sources.

conscription.rationale: Cobden wanted standing armaments cut and condemned war, so compulsory military service is rejected.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Bright campaigned for the vote, so voice mattered; exit as a larger check was not stated.

state-as-business.rationale: Retrenchment fits business-like thrift, but citizens-as-customers is a modern public-choice idea.

positive-liberty.rationale: Bright rejected state regulation to secure workers' conditions, treating freedom as absence of interference.

media-academia-power.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement valued press freedom.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Cobden and Bright were anti-slavery and universalist; racial genetics debates came later.

organic-representation.rationale: Bright pursued individual franchise extension and ballots, opposing representation by estates and communities.

total-state.rationale: The school's laissez-faire and minimal-state outlook is the opposite of the totalitarian state.

national-rebirth.rationale: Cobden's internationalism and peace outlook has no place for radical national regeneration.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Cobden opposed colonialism and the Opium War as unrighteous, and Bright opposed meddling abroad.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The movement attacked privilege and championed impersonal markets and law.

bound-labor.rationale: The movement was anti-slavery and for free labour; Cobden called for an unfettered labour market.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Classical liberals trusted reason and economic science; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Cobden's cosmopolitanism points to universal principles, but not stated as epistemology.

single-common-good.rationale: The school saw good arising from voluntary exchange and competing interests; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred; business governance by owners is assumed.

school-vouchers.rationale: Cobden promoted popular education through voluntary British schools, but vouchers are anachronistic.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Retrenchment and public thrift were declared pillars of the school, as Hirst's preface describes thrift as the buttress of free trade.

economic-freedom.rationale: The school tied commercial freedom to political and social reform and peace; Cobden called himself a free-trader first.

rule-by-example.rationale: The movement favoured written law and parliamentary government, not reliance on rulers' virtue.

national-self-determination.rationale: Cobden opposed intervention in other nations' affairs, which fits self-government, but did not state this principle.

force-without-un.rationale: Cobden opposed using ships of war to coerce other nations; Bright criticised the Crimean War, so use of force abroad is rejected.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Many in the school were nonconformist Christians; the school as such took no position.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare was not an object; no documented position.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from Poor Law-era liberal thrift; not documented in the sources.

class-collaboration.rationale: Cobden and Bright stressed the shared interest of manufacturers and workers in cheap food and free trade.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cobden founded the Manchester Athenaeum, and the school valued education, so sacrificing libraries is rejected.

dominated-front.rationale: Cobden's cosmopolitan free-trade outlook is not anti-Western; inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: Not a working-class organising question; Cobden favoured international fraternity through commerce.

ban-interest.rationale: Free commerce and credit were assumed; usury bans had long been repealed under classical liberalism.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Bright backed the Union over slavery, treating slavery as the central moral issue; legal racial caste is rejected.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Cobden did see the aristocratic landed class using the state through the Corn Laws, but not as a general theory.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from industrial growth and market allocation.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy theory with no place in the school; inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: Bright favoured seat redistribution and secret ballot, but PR was not on their agenda.

national-mission.rationale: Cobden's non-intervention and opposition to empire reject spreading one's government abroad by force.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Cobden condemned the Corn Law politics as factious and landed interest as self-serving, but this was not a general claim.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics postdates the school and contradicts its liberalism.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The school applied laissez-faire to government policy, though Cobden accepted legislation protecting children and women, so not strict.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Inferred from universalism and anti-slavery; not discussed.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Bright treated slavery as the central moral issue in the American Civil War, and the school was anti-slavery.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not relevant to the school; no position.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Bright and Cobden doubted the value of colonies, but the statement concerns a historical characterisation not addressed.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Church-state separation and press freedom imply religious liberty, so restricting conversion is rejected.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred from opposition to religiously motivated state restrictions.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Church-state separation fits, but the educational debates are not documented in the sources I opened.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not applicable to the school; a growing state is contrary to its views.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Bright pressed for franchise extension and secret ballot, and Cobden backed the Charter's working-man vote committee.

trade-surplus.rationale: Cobden said to buy in the cheapest market and sell in the dearest, and held that import freedom helps the public, rejecting mercantilist export surpluses.

population-transfer.rationale: Inferred from liberal individual rights and opposition to coercion.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Cobden rejected coercion by arms ("Away with all attempts to coerce any nation"), though that concerns states and not all individuals.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The school favoured commercial competition, but struggle between peoples was rejected, so a split reading.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Press freedom and open agitation point against banning parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Cobden's attacks on aristocratic privilege fit partly, but republican freedom theory is not documented.

separated-powers.rationale: Inferred from limited-government liberalism; the movement's tool was Parliament.

vanguard-party.rationale: The movement was mass reformist agitation, not vanguardism; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Cobden did argue the bread tax falls on the poor, but the school did not demand institutions prioritise them.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Bright opposed state regulation of wages and conditions; whether the school wanted strikes limited is not documented.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Malthusian ideas were discussed in classical economics, but the sources show no school position.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Cosmopolitanism points against, though not documented.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred; the school pursued elections and extending the franchise.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The school opposed war and executive licence; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Cobden argued the price of food is fixed by the market, and the Corn Laws were a tax; price fixing contradicts his case.

party-controls-media.rationale: Freedom of the press was one of the school's listed commitments.

party-commands-army.rationale: Cobden wanted armaments cut and opposed military political power; inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Cobden called himself neither Whig nor Tory; he valued independent judgment. Inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Cobden wanted minimal intercourse between governments and more among peoples; a supranational union is not documented.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Cobden's focus was on parliamentary control of finance and war; inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Bright favoured disestablishment of the Church; church governance by bishops was not their issue.

clerical-rule.rationale: Separation of church and state is a stated commitment, rejecting rule by clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Bright and Cobden opposed the Crimean War and attacked their own government's policy, yet did not advocate working for defeat.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Press freedom was a stated commitment; inferred for art.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Non-intervention and opposition to balance-of-power diplomacy imply ending permanent alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inferred from commerce and property freedom; a ban on renting is incompatible.

people-in-arms.rationale: Cobden wanted armaments reduced and favoured passive resistance; a citizen army was not their proposal.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The school represented industrial towns against the landed interest; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cosmopolitan outlook suggests it, but not documented.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no documented position.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from rationalist liberal outlook; undiscussed.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious liberty is implied by separation of church and state; undiscussed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's liberalism is related, but the school itself did not state this.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Cobden said lending to governments for armies is wrong, yet property in debts was respected; cancellation is not proposed. Inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Cobden tied prosperity to freedom and free trade, so a trade-off is rejected.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Cobden wanted retrenchment and non-intervention; aid is anachronistic.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Cobden wanted mutual disarmament and reduced armaments; inferred for nuclear.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Peace over territory is implied by the school's pacifism; undiscussed.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The school saw property as a right in itself; inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not relevant to the school; no position.

collective-defense.rationale: Cobden opposed entangling alliances and balance-of-power diplomacy.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Cobden opposed colonialism and Bright opposed meddling in Egypt; inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The school sought separation, not state control of religion.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Bright backed the Union against secession in the US but Cobden had no stated view.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Church-state separation and the movement's attack on privilege reject sacred rulers.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The sources do not discuss progressive versus flat rates.

character-from-environment.rationale: Cobden pointed to distress, disease and crime resulting from conditions, but this is not stated as a general theory.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Parliamentary reformism and rights-based liberalism rejects lawless sovereignty.

land-redistribution.rationale: Cobden attacked landed privilege but did not propose seizure; inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Opposed to territorial expansion and coercion.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Press freedom and church-state separation reject it.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from liberal opposition to state coercion.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Cobden's internationalism was universal, not ethnic; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Cobden stressed commercial interests, but the school did not offer a theory of history.

ban-cartels.rationale: Hostility to privilege and monopoly (Corn Laws) fits, though state action against cartels is not documented.

no-bailouts.rationale: Retrenchment and public thrift imply opposing public support for failing firms; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not addressed; no position beyond liberalism.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from laissez-faire opposition to quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Cobden opposed protection and held foreign markets fix home prices, rejecting autarkic blocs.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Bright opposed regulation of working conditions; binding standards in trade treaties are anachronistic.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Cobden's campaigns targeted landed aristocratic privilege such as the Corn Laws.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Cobden opposed colonialism and Bright urged India reform toward eventual independence.

patriotic-education.rationale: Cobden's cosmopolitanism points against teaching national pride; undiscussed.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from private commerce.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The school's confidence in commerce implies it; undiscussed.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Cobden opposed empire and Bright opposed meddling abroad.

delink-world-market.rationale: Cobden's whole programme was integration through free trade.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Marxist framing outside the school; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from freedom of association and property, but anachronistic.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Their reform strategy was parliamentary; entrenchment was not discussed.

elective-rulers.rationale: Bright advocated an extended franchise and the ballot, and Cobden supported inquiry into the Charter.

minority-veto.rationale: Not addressed; the school used parliamentary majorities.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Cobden and Bright worked through the House of Commons and sought reform there.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The school attacked landed privilege rather than endorsing paternal duty of the wealthy.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Cobden and Bright were career agitators and MPs, committed to political action.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Anachronistic; Marxist-inspired framing alien to the school.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Cobden treated trade as mutually beneficial.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred; the school stressed equal rights.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Opposed war for territory; inferred from pacifism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Bright treated slavery as the central moral issue of the American Civil War.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Cobden wanted armaments cut and opposed militarism.

office-by-exam.rationale: Cobden's attack on aristocratic privilege and patronage suggests merit appointment; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Cobden opposed protectionism and favoured open commerce.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Not their model; MPs acted on independent judgment.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from thrift and self-reliance; anachronistic.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Private property in land was assumed though landlord privilege was attacked.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Cobden pressed retrenchment and parliamentary control of finance; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Opposed to restriction in commerce; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Bright and Cobden opposed intervention abroad.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from press freedom and open exchange.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from free exchange and property.

job-guarantee.rationale: Cobden argued the labour market works best if left unfettered.

democratic-peace.rationale: Cobden linked trade to peace, not democracy; he rejected force to spread any system.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Reformers pursued change through law and Parliament; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Non-intervention was a founding policy of Cobden and Bright, including opposition to foreign interference in other states.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Press freedom and open Parliament; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement was organised as the Anti-Corn Law League.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Cobden favoured arbitration yet minimal intergovernmental dealings; split.

religion-illusion.rationale: Many were devout nonconformists; no position as a school.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The school turned classical economic liberalism into policy and held commerce brought progress.

treaties-binding.rationale: Cobden negotiated a trade treaty with France and valued agreements.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic but contrary to liberal truth-seeking; inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from opposition to state interference; anachronistic.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Free press and open agitation were the school's method.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Cobden opposed colonialism; colonies brought little trade.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Cobden called himself neither Whig nor Tory but a free-trader.

social-market-economy.rationale: Bright opposed state regulation of work conditions.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Cobden wanted large cuts and arbitration, but not abolition.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Non-intervention and rejection of balance of power diplomacy.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not their model. (inferred from core principles)

property-franchise.rationale: Bright pushed franchise extension to most of the working class.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Press freedom treated as sufficient; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule of law; inferred from liberal constitutionalism.

racial-franchise.rationale: Bright's moral stance against slavery and for broad suffrage.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Cobden attacked the Corn Laws as a tax on food and argued that foreign markets fix home prices, rejecting protection of domestic producers.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The school applied laissez-faire to policy and favoured retrenchment, so state steering of investment is opposed (inferred, not directly discussed).

widespread-small-property.rationale: Cobden attacked landed privilege and addressed tenant farmers, but a programme of spreading small property is not documented.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Cobden saw rising trade and prosperity as beneficial; the claim is anachronistic and undiscussed.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Adherents were split: Cobden and Bright attacked the landed aristocracy's monopoly as a threat to liberty, yet rejected levelling taxes and regulation.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the school's emphasis on individual liberty and limited state interference in private life.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The school sought separation of church and state and minimal government, which implies state neutrality in belief and no state-run campaign for or against religion.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the night-watchman state in which police, courts and prisons remain a core function of limited government.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from the school's push to widen the franchise on majority principles, with no sign of guaranteed communal shares.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The school opposed state regulation and welfare-type provision as interference, so private and voluntary effort was the preferred route.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the school's trust in the voters' free choice of representatives.

vote-delegation.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the school's reliance on representative parliamentary government and widened suffrage.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the emphasis on retrenchment and minimal state spending over large public programmes.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Bright's Quaker background and the school's opposition to state control of religion, so churches set their own offices.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the mid-Victorian norms of the period, which the school did not challenge.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Cobden and Bright campaigned for wider suffrage among citizens; the school never addressed non-citizen residents, so this is left split.

rent-control.rationale: Bright rejected state regulation of wages and factories, so a legal rent cap is inferred to fall under the same laissez-faire objection.

abolish-ip.rationale: The school opposed monopolies and protection, but nothing in the sources addresses patents or copyright; adherents could go either way.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Cobden's peace speeches attacked military spending and militarism, so drilled national-service youth movements are inferred to be opposed.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from Cobden's opposition to armaments and foreign entanglement; nuclear weapons were unknown to the school.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Cobden urged non-intervention and minimal political entanglement abroad, which implies opposing foreign garrisons on home soil.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The sources do not touch genocide recognition; a principled moral stance and a non-intervention bias pull in opposite directions.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Cobden attacked landlord rents under the Corn Laws, but the school defended capital and profit as legitimate returns, so it is split.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Bright, a Quaker, leaned toward pacifism, but the school opposed war as policy rather than denying a right of defence; inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: A cosmopolitan commercial creed is inferred to have had little interest in mythic national continuity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Anachronistic: the school did not address sex or gender, and a Victorian liberal would be inferred to treat sex as natural.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Anachronistic: no sourced view on feminist theory; Cobden's limited openness on women's legal protection does not settle it.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The school condemned military glory and war as wasteful, so honouring war dead as martyrs and saints is inferred to be rejected.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The school favoured separation of church and state and commerce-led pragmatism, so a cosmic good-versus-evil politics is inferred to be foreign to it.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; a free-trading, individualist creed has no stated view on diaspora homelands.

culture-before-state.rationale: Not addressed; the school's priorities were commerce and reform, not national cultural renewal.

god-not-male.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed; nothing in the sources bears on how God is described.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed in the sources.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Cobden's free-trade speeches argued for open exchange regardless of nationality, so reserving the economy for a national majority is inferred to be opposed.

independent-unions.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the school's wish to keep government out of economic life, which favours free association over state-run labour bodies.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The school never took up socialism; inferred from its belief that prosperity comes from free exchange rather than from class power.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Retrenchment pointed against state provision, yet Manchester's own civic liberals ran municipal utilities; inferred and split.

second-chamber.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Cobden and Bright's hostility to the aristocratic House of Lords and their push for wider suffrage.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from the school's defence of private property and free enterprise against state or collective control.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the school's preference for individual and national self-government over new layers of collective administration.

family-wage.rationale: Bright held wages are for owners and workers to settle, so a family-sized wage is not something to set by norm or law; inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the belief that less regulation and freer enterprise serve the public.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from retrenchment and opposition to government spending beyond essentials.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the school's defence of individual liberty and freedom of commerce against state interference.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the school's support for press freedom and individual liberty against state control.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from the school's individualism and minimal-government principle that the state serves individuals; the sources do not state this wording.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Bright was a Quaker, but the school separated church from state and kept politics to commerce and peace; inferred and split.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents could favour either central uniformity or local self-rule.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the school's faith in free enterprise and technical progress to lower costs.

dense-cities.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed; the school's free-trade urbanising industry gives no clear stance.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred from the school's universalist, cosmopolitan free-trade outlook and Bright and Cobden's anti-slavery stance.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from the school's cosmopolitan internationalism, which put common humanity and commerce above national or group identity.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Cobden's peace speech and the school's opposition to military spending, empire and foreign intervention leave armed force for defence only.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred: the school's cosmopolitan free-trade outlook treated nations as commercial partners and did not define them by language, though it never addressed the question.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from its support for wider suffrage on equal individual terms and for separating church and state.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: Cobden and Bright attacked scares about foreign enemies as pretexts for military spending, so they would treat such claims as exaggerated.

free-public-college.rationale: Anachronistic; the school favoured minimal government and low taxation and opposed state provision, though it never addressed university tuition.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Anachronistic; the school's minimal-government, low-tax stance would oppose new taxes and regulation alike, and environmental policy was not discussed.

future-generations.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources do not address environmental duties, and adherents' prosperity-through-trade outlook points both ways.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred: the school argued from individual rights and commerce, not gendered values, though Cobden's peace advocacy drew on some such appeals.

arms-reduction.rationale: The school opposed military spending and advocated retrenchment and peace through commerce, and Cobden argued for mutual reduction of armaments; the cited peace speech is the primary source.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from Cobden's opposition to aristocratic foreign policy and secrecy in foreign affairs; the cited sources do not state it directly.

capital-controls.rationale: Free trade and minimal government were central, and the school opposed state interference in commerce, so limits on cross-border money would run against its core; no source discusses capital flows directly.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: security and defence were among the few functions the school left to a minimal state.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Cobden opposed war and military spending but through persuasion and politics, not mutiny; inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Bright rejected state regulation of wages and conditions and was hostile to coercive union action; the school favoured individual contracts.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: income top-ups funded by taxation contradict its low taxation and minimal-government principles.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: it championed retrenchment and low public spending, though it preferred political pressure to legal rules.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: It sought universal free trade on equal terms rather than rules tilted towards any group of countries.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Inferred: the school pursued reform through suffrage extension and Parliament, not overthrow.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: it held a definite blueprint of free trade and laissez-faire rather than pluralism of economic systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its aversion to state-directed economic intervention and valuation schemes.

sacred-nation.rationale: Cobden's cosmopolitan appeal to peace through commerce is hostile to sacralising the nation.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its opposition to state provision and to redistribution through taxation.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: it explained inequality by Corn Law privilege and not by regional exploitation, and rejected the analogy of colonial rule.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred: its appeals to individual liberty and common interest of nations assume universal human interests.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: it backed press freedom but opposed state funding of institutions as interference.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The school favoured separation of church and state and religious liberty without taking a view on whether religions share one truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: The Anti-Corn Law League existed to end protection and price support for agriculture, and Cobden argued that free trade in corn would serve all.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Cobden's opposition to military spending and armaments races, though it would not endorse unilateral risk-taking by rhetoric alone.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred from the school's belief in a harmony of interests between classes and its coalition of manufacturers and workers behind free trade.

ban-fgm.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its liberal defence of individual bodily rights, though it was wary of state intervention in custom.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its liberal individualism and equal legal rights, though the school did not campaign on women's property.

one-language-many-names.rationale: A linguistic classification question the school never addressed.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its minimal-government preference and property-rights liberalism, which favours legal redress over agency regulation.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to hereditary privilege and aristocratic influence over lawmaking, and its demand for wider elected suffrage.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its priority on individual economic liberty and minimal state interference.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from its general liberalism and distrust of state coercion; sentencing policy was not its concern.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its laissez-faire preference against state-imposed requirements and its free movement of people and goods.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from laissez-faire and freedom of contract in labour, which favour voluntary association over compelled membership or dues.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from the school's push for wider suffrage; the issue itself was not addressed.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The school backed separation of church and state and ending the Established Church's privileges, so no interpretation would have legal precedence.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from its support for representative government and wider suffrage, with a focus on limited government over popular rule.

premarital-sex.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from mid-Victorian moral norms, though the school left private morals largely to individuals.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from its defence of press freedom and its distrust of state power over the individual.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Anachronistic; the school opposed state welfare and wage regulation, so a state-run income guarantee would have been resisted.

women-suffrage.rationale: The school wanted wider suffrage but women's suffrage was not its cause, and adherents were not clearly of one view.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from its church-state separation stance, which did not frame religion as a cause of women's status.

race-social-construct.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its belief that free trade would unite peoples and its opposition to empire and conquest.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from its minimal-government and retrenchment principles, which oppose new state bodies.

missingStatements.text: Governments should cut military and naval spending sharply in peacetime.
missingStatements.rationale: Cobden argued for cutting enormous standing armaments and moved in 1851 for mutual reduction of armaments.

missingStatements.text: Disputes between states should be settled by international arbitration rather than war.
missingStatements.rationale: Cobden proposed international arbitration in Parliament in 1849 and urged referring disputes to arbitrators.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to arbitration as a peace mechanism; overlaps non-intervention and empower-international-orgs and does not justify a new statement.

missingStatements.text: Tariffs on imported food should be abolished.
missingStatements.rationale: Repeal of the Corn Laws was the movement's defining campaign, as a tax falling hardest on the poor.

missingStatements.text: Countries should not acquire or keep overseas colonies.
missingStatements.rationale: Cobden opposed colonialism and Little Englander views held colonies brought little benefit.

notes: Cobden accepted protective legislation for children and women; Bright opposed the 1847 Ten Hours Act. Many answers on modern topics are low-confidence inferences.
